prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the molecular-glue mechanism of cereblon.

statement.case_for: Seven of eight members place B029 in their top three and it is the only candidate that survives every different lens in the room. Chemically it is a new principle, event-driven and catalytic induced proximity, rather than an incremental improvement of an existing modality. The mechanism has been confirmed independently by many groups and with structures of ternary complexes. It spans two strands that explain each other: the designed heterobifunctional PROTAC (Crews, Deshaies) and the mechanistic explanation of thalidomide-type molecular glues through cereblon (Handa). Keeping Handa in the configuration is my way of making the prize about the principle and not only about one compound class. After the opening round I move it above my own first choice, B027, because it has the widest support and a defensible three-name core.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is real. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim all have credible claims, and the three-name cap forces choices that colleagues rank differently: three of the opening ballots pick Ciulli over Handa or over Deshaies. Clinical maturity is also incomplete because approved degraders are still few, and a committee that prefers vindication in the clinic could reasonably wait. Finally, the PROTAC and glue strands arose separately, so a single citation may blur two different histories.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B029 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that the glue/cereblon strand is a distinct lineage that the three-name cap leaves out, and that recognition is timely.
responses.response: I agree on timing and on Crews and Deshaies as the founding pair, but I disagree about leaving the glue strand out. Handa's identification of cereblon is what turned thalidomide from an empirical drug into a mechanistic example and showed that degradation can be induced by a monovalent molecule. Without that strand the prize reads as a story about bifunctional linkers only. Ciulli's contribution to ternary-complex structure and VHL ligands is the strongest alternative third name, and I would accept it if the committee decides the prize should be about rational design instead of mechanism of action.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks halide perovskites (B058) first for the clear physics of defect tolerance and the rapid rise in efficiency, and ranks B029 second with the caveat that no PROTAC drug is approved.
responses.response: I ranked B058 only eighth. The efficiency rise is remarkable, but the credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok is very contested, and stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, which makes the maturity case thinner than for degraders. I take the point on clinical approval for B029, but for chemistry I weigh the mechanistic and design principle more than regulatory status, and that principle is established. I would want to see how the chair proposes to settle the perovskite three-name split before I treat it as a competitive configuration.

responses.point: Zou ranks base editing (B047) first, on the grounds that deaminase engineering is an original chemical invention that is already in clinical use, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli credited.
responses.response: I find the base editor invention elegant and I did put it close to my list, but I have two reservations. It is built on the CRISPR-Cas9 platform recognised in 2020, so the prize narrative would be an extension of a recent prize, and the independent deaminase-fusion work of Kondo and Nishida complicates an exclusive Liu-centred claim. I think B029 has the cleaner claim to be a new field, but I would not oppose B047 as a serious alternative if the round shows it has more first-place support than I now see.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler's long-range electron transfer in proteins (B056) first, valuing the quantitative physical framework for respiration and photosynthesis, and ranks B029 second.
responses.response: We have sat together since 2015 and I respect the argument that B056 gives a clear quantitative picture. My concern is that Marcus theory was recognised in 1992, so the committee must be convinced that the protein-specific tunnelling and hopping maps are a distinct achievement and not an experimental elaboration of it. It has also drawn one first-place vote and little else, so it looks unlikely to reach five votes. I would want to hear what new principle you see beyond confirmation of Marcus theory in proteins.

uncertainties: Whether the third name should be Handa (mechanism of molecular glues) or Ciulli (rational design, VHL, ternary-complex structure); the opening ballots are split.
Whether a PROTAC and molecular-glue citation can be written as one achievement without implying that Sakamoto, Gray and Ito were overlooked.
Whether the committee accepts the absence of an approved degrader as a reason to wait, which I cannot resolve from the files alone.
Whether the support for B027 (Car-Parrinello) can grow beyond my own and the chair's ranking; I have not verified the claims in the opening ballots independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted ballot. My postdoc collaboration with Arieh Warshel concerns EVB methods, and Warshel is not credited on any shortlisted candidate. My own work on ligand-binding free energies and enzyme simulation is adjacent to B027 and to the computational side of drug discovery, but involves no personal tie to the credited names.
